title: Embed shell scripts in a generated pipeline file

blocks.text: The pipeline file of the monorepo is generated: each step runs a shell script kept in `ci/`, and the generator copies the script into the step's YAML `run: |` block. The generated file is checked in and compared byte for byte with the previous one, and a YAML linter that rejects any line ending in whitespace runs before every merge. The scripts are edited by many people, on Linux, macOS and Windows, some pasted from indented documentation. Each edit made the generated file change in ways nobody intended.
Finish `runBlock(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/PipelineStep.java`. `render(...)` already puts what it returns under `run: |`.

When you're done, every script line sits six spaces in, keeping its indentation relative to the script's other lines; the result is the same whether or not the file ends with a line break and whichever line endings it uses; and nothing the linter rejects reaches the file. Every line of the result, the last one included, ends with `\n`. About four lines in total.

cases.says: a step's script appears under run: at six spaces, keeping its own nesting, and the step ends with a line break
indentation common to every line of the script is replaced, not added to
a script file that ends with a line break loses its common indentation too
blank lines of the script are empty in the generated file, with no indentation on them
a script saved with Windows line endings gives the same file, with no carriage returns
whitespace at the end of a script line does not reach the generated file

origin.section: At Run Time, Indentation Is Your Job: indent() and stripIndent()

concepts: indent(n) adds n spaces to every line, blank lines included, normalises line terminators to \n and ends the result with one.
stripIndent() counts the last line even if blank, so text that ends with a line break keeps its common indentation.
